$25, his hurt being that of severe burns. This is a case where the doctor made a special reduction in hope of getting the
money, and if the aforesaid position is taken in deducting the grant, we should also add at least $25 to the doctor's fees.

Of course I recognize that our application is not in the nature of a demand but that, of asking a special grant, and
would ask your most generous consideration in view of the financial needs of the work.



Thanking you in anticipation of your favour, I am,


Yours sincerely,
T.E. BARTON, Sec.-Treas.


W.E. DITCHBURN, Chief Inspector of Indian Agencies, Victoria, B.C.

Vote 276, Indians of British Columbia: Grant towards Rebuilding St. George's Hospital, Alert Bay


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, August 22, 1924.

SIR, - I have received a copy of an Order in Council (P.C. 2498), dated December 22nd, 1923, authorizing the
payment from your vote for Indians of British Columbia of the sum of $5,000 as a contribution towards the cost of
rebuilding St. George's Hospital, conducted by the Columbia Coast Mission, Inc., at Alert Bay, B.C., which was
destroyed by fire on August 18th, 1923.

I beg to point out that while this institution may be of considerable benefit to the Indians of British Columbia it has no
direct connection with the management of the Indians, other than acting in the ordinary capacity of Medical Officer,
for which a salary of $850 a year is paid by your department; they are also paid at the rate of $1 a day for the Indian
patients treated in the hospital.

I am of opinion that all grants for which no accounting is made to the Dominion Government should be specially
provided for by Parliament.


I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.


The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs.



NOTE. - No reply had been received to the above letter up to the time of printing.

Vote 278, General: Allowance to Commissioner W.M. Graham for use of Automobile


AUDITOR GENERALS OFFICE, November 19, 1924.

SIR, - I find in the course of the examination of the accounts in support of your expenditure for the fiscal year 1923 -
24, that Mr. W.M. Graham, commissioner at Regina, was paid $60 a month as an allowance for the use of his own
automobile, except from October 9th to February 29th, during which period he was paid on a basis of the trips actually
made by him.

<!-- page 562 -->
Kindly advise me as to your authority for paying this allowance to Mr. Graham, and also as to the calculation on
which the amount of the allowance is based.

I might point out that both a chauffeur and a garage are provided Mr. Graham out of public moneys in addition to the
above allowance.


I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.


The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs.

<!-- page 563 -->
Vote 279, Indian Education: Payment of Removal Expenses of Teachers


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, February 2, 1924.

SIR, - My attention has been drawn to the fact that in a few cases a teacher, on appointment to an Indian school, has
been allowed his expenses from his former place of residence to his place of employment.

I have been given to understand, by your School Branch, that these expenses are allowed in only a few cases in British
Columbia, where the school is situated in a remote locality, as it would be difficult to obtain a teacher willing to take a
position in such localities, unless his expenses there were paid by your department.

I beg to point out that it is not the rule to allow an appointee to any position in, the public service his expenses from
his place of residence to the place of his employment. When for any special reason it may be considered advisable to
allow such expenses, they cannot be regarded as ordinary travelling expenses on official duty, but must be considered
as being of the nature of removal expenses, and as such require the authority of the Treasury Board.


I am, Sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.


The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs.


DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, February 7, 1924.

DEAR MR. KEARNS, - I have your letter of the 2nd instant, relative to removal expenses in the case of teachers of
Indian Schools, and in reply I wish to state that the attention of the Superintendent of Indian Education has been drawn
to the regulations concerning this matter. In future, the authority of the Treasury Board will be secured if it is found
necessary to pay the removal expenses of teachers in our employ.


Yours very truly,
D.C. SCOTT, D.S.G.


The Assistant Auditor General.

Vote 279, Indian Education: Payments to Inspector of Construction at Fraser Lake Boarding School


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, February 25, 1924.

SIR, - I beg to ask your attention to the payments made by you to Mr. Myles Morley, as Inspector of Construction at
the Fraser Lake Indian Boarding School, since July, 1922.

Mr. Morley was paid during the fiscal year 1922 - 23 for 224 days at $6 a day, being for every day included in the
period from July 16th, 1922, to February 28th, 1923, with the exception of 4 -days in July. During the current. fiscal
year he has been paid continuously at the same rate from March 1st to May 31st. On looking over the returns for
previous years I find that Mr. Morley was paid continuously at the same rate, from October 15th, 1919, to
February 22nd, 1922, while engaged on inspection work on other schools.

<!-- page 564 -->
The rates established in the Classification List for the position of Inspector of Construction are: -

Monthly - $100, $105, $110, etc., to $140.

Daily - Prevailing rates not exceeding $7 for services as required.



I understand this to mean that when the employment is not Continuous the inspector may be paid up to $7 a day for
those days only on which he is actually engaged on the work, but that when the employment is continuous the monthly
rates Shall apply. The prevailing rates paid during any month should not exceed the maximum monthly rate of $140.

I should also like to ask your attention to the dates on which the certificates for Mr. Morley's employment were issued
by the Civil Service Commission. On February 9th, 1923, a certificate for his employment for six months from
July 16th, 1922, was issued, and on the same date a second certificate extending his employment to March 16th was
issued; again on June 19th a certificate was issued further extending his employment to July 16th. As Mr. Morley
received his pay regularly month by month it would appear that his pay cheques were issued in,a number of cases prior
to the authorization of his employment. I trust you will take steps to prevent the recurrence of a like irregularity in the
future.


I am, Sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.


The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs.


DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, February 27, 1924.

DEAR SIR, - I beg to acknowledge the receipt of your letter of the 25th instant, with reference to payments made by
this Department to Mr. Myles Morley as Inspector of Construction at the Fraser Lake Indian boarding school since
July, 1922. I have noted what you say, that is, that when an Inspector of Construction is employed continuously during
the month his services should be paid at the monthly rate.

In reply I beg to say that the certificates of temporary appointment were issued by the Civil Service Commission for
certain specified periods with remuneration at the rate of $6 per day. No mention was made of a monthly rate, and the
Department paid at the rate which was provided for in the certificates. However, in the future we will be guided by
your interpretation of the regulations, and, in employing men as Inspectors of Construction, we will specify that they
are to be paid at the rate of $6 per day, but that their monthly remuneration must not exceed $140, the maximum
provided under the classification schedule.

The last paragraph of your letter has been noted.


Yours very truly,
D.C. SCOTT, D.S.G.


The Assistant Auditor General.

Vote 279, Indian Education: Payments to Wyatt-Ireland, Limited, for repairs to Elkhorn Indian School


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, May 23, 1924.
